issues.description: The problem statement and the solution Dockerfile expect a start.sh script to be present and executable (instructions to COPY start.sh and CMD ./start.sh), but neither the template repository nor the solution repository contains a start.sh file. This is a structural mismatch: Dockerfiles in the artifacts assume the presence of a repository file that does not exist, which will prevent building/running the Docker image as described and will confuse students following the deployment instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Include a start.sh script in the repository (with the expected behavior and executable permissions) or modify the Dockerfile and problem statement to not rely on start.sh (e.g., use ENTRYPOINT ["java","-jar","/app/app.jar"] or similar). Ensure the Dockerfile, the problem text, and the repository contents consistently reference the same startup mechanism.
